propositions: The completion verifier returns non-deterministic verdicts (PASS vs FAIL with identical inputs, code, and acceptance criteria) within minutes of identical runs, making the close gate unreliable in both directions (spurious FAIL blocks legitimate work; spurious PASS admits incomplete work).

The verifier's non-determinism is concentrated on test-existence crediting: it marks criteria unmet claiming tests do not exist when they provably do, due to fallible free-form search strategy and variable semantic/regex queries rather than literal substring and ticket-id lookup.

The COMPLETION_VERDICT sidecar lacks sufficient context (no verified_at_sha, trace_id, coverage, input snapshot) to distinguish genuine non-determinism from input drift, preventing diagnosability of stored records.
The verifier runs with unpinned LLM temperature, allowing sampling variance to flip borderline judgments; pinning temperature to 0 (greedy decoding) reduces but does not eliminate variance.

Accepting criteria phrased '...—regression test' or '...—guard test' are vulnerable to false-negative test-existence judgments because the verifier's search strategy does not systematically use ticket-id or list_directory before concluding absence.

The completion verifier must record verified_at_sha and trace_id in both PASS and FAIL sidecar payloads, pin LLM temperature to 0 by default (unless REBAR_LLM_TEMPERATURE is explicitly set), and update prompt guidance to mandate literal-substring search and ticket-id lookup for test-existence judgments.
